passages.original: aut, Ego et Pater unus est1: sed cum dicit, Ego et Pater unum sumus; utrumque audi, et unum, et sumus, et a Charybdi et a Scylla liberaberis. In duobus istis verbis quod dixit, unum, liberat te ab Ario : quod dixit, sumus, liberat te a Sabellio. Si unum, non ergp diversum; si sumus, : ergo et Pater et Filius. Sumus enim, non diceret de uno; sed et unum non diceret de diverso. Ergo ideo verum est, ipquit, judicium meum, breviter ut audias, quia Filius Dei sum.
passages.english: or, "I and the Father is one"; but when he says, "I and the Father are one," listen to both, both "one" and "are," and you will be freed both from Charybdis and from Scylla. In these two words, his saying "one" frees you from Arius; his saying "are" frees you from Sabellius. If "one," then not different; if "are," then both Father and Son. For he would not say "are" of one; but neither would he say "one" of what is different. Therefore my judgement is true, he says, so that you may hear it briefly, because I am the Son of God.
passages.notes: The "1" after "unus est" is a footnote mark and has been omitted. Scanning errors corrected: "ergp" read as "ergo", "ipquit" as "inquit". The stray colon after "si sumus" has been disregarded.

passages.original: Innumerabiles enim sunt, qui se videmes non solum jactant, sed a Christo illuminatos videri volunt : sunt autem hæretici. Forte ipsi per januam intrave- runt? Absit. Sabellius dicit, Qni Filius est, ipse est Pater : sed si Filius, non est Pater. Non intrat per ostium, qui Filium dicit Patrem. Arius dicit : Aliud est Pater, aliud est Filius, Recte diceret, si diceret Alius; non, aliud, Quando enim dicit, Aliud, ei contradicit a quo audit, Ego et Puter unum sumus (Joan. x, 30). Nec ipse ergo per ostium intrat: prædicat enim Christum qualem sibi fingit, non qualem veritas dicit.
passages.english: For there are countless people who not only boast that they see, but want to appear to have been enlightened by Christ; yet they are heretics. Have they perhaps entered through the door? Far from it. Sabellius says, "He who is the Son is himself the Father"; but if [he is] Son, he is not Father. He who calls the Son the Father does not enter through the door. Arius says, "The Father is one thing, the Son another thing." He would speak rightly if he said "another [person]," not "another thing." For when he says "another thing," he contradicts the one from whom he hears, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30). So neither does he enter through the door, for he preaches a Christ such as he invents for himself, not such as the truth declares.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "videmes" read as "videntes", "Qni" as "Qui", "Puter" as "Pater". Augustine contrasts Latin "alius" (another person, masculine) with "aliud" (another thing, neuter, implying a difference of nature).
